title: A visit to Samsung’s massive new semiconductor hub
gist: A dispatch from Samsung's Pyeongtaek chip complex: three fabs run around the clock, a fourth is coming online, and a fifth, halted in the 2024 memory downturn, restarted when AI demand surged. Samsung expects memory demand to keep climbing through 2028 and is using the build-out to win back HBM share from SK Hynix. On-site construction labor earns about 140,000 won ($97) a day and expects years of work.

insights.claim: Samsung's Pyeongtaek complex has three fabs operating around the clock and a fourth coming online, on a campus about the size of New York's Central Park.
insights.speaker: Michelle Kim
insights.so_what: New memory capacity is coming in steps, so track fab 4 ramp timing for effects on HBM/DRAM supply and pricing.

insights.claim: Construction of Samsung's fifth Pyeongtaek fab stopped during the 2024 memory-chip demand slump and restarted when the AI boom sent demand soaring. Memory capex is turning on and off with AI demand signals.
insights.speaker: Michelle Kim
insights.so_what: Memory remains cyclical: capex restarts tied to AI raise the risk of oversupply if AI demand cools after 2028.
insights.locator: Construction of a fifth was halted

insights.claim: Samsung predicts that demand for memory chips will keep surging through 2028.
insights.speaker: Michelle Kim
insights.so_what: This is the planning horizon behind the capex: a bullish memory cycle at least to 2028, according to Samsung.
insights.quote: Samsung predicts that demand for memory chips will continue to surge through 2028.

insights.claim: For years Samsung watched domestic rival SK Hynix pull ahead in high-bandwidth memory for Nvidia's AI accelerators, and the Pyeongtaek build-out is Samsung's attempt to win back the lead in memory. Meanwhile TSMC dominates the foundry business.
insights.speaker: Michelle Kim
insights.so_what: Watch HBM qualification and market share at Nvidia: added Samsung capacity threatens SK Hynix's pricing power.
insights.locator: And for years the company watched

themes.theme: AI boom labor economics on site

insights.claim: A safety officer at the Pyeongtaek fab construction site earns 140,000 won ($97) a day. She says pay is higher than at other construction sites and expects the boom to keep her busy for some time.
insights.speaker: Michelle Kim
insights.so_what: This is a ground-level sign that the AI capex boom is tightening local construction labor markets in Korea.
insights.locator: Although the heat can be brutal

insights.claim: Thousands of construction workers, many shuttled in from Songtan, are reshaping Pyeongtaek's local economy. Banners advertise short-term studio leases, and the real-estate offices serving contractors also sell homes to salaried Samsung engineers.
insights.speaker: Michelle Kim
insights.so_what: AI-driven fab buildouts are spilling into regional property and services demand.
insights.locator: They walk to lunch, sweaty and flushed
